Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP Product recalls 40,000 bottles of eye drops across the US recalled over issues with sterility of product Prestige Brand Holdings has voluntarily recalled a batch of its Clear Eyes eye drops after FDA alert Marina Dunbar Sat 22 Aug 2026 11.44 EDT Last modified on Sat 22 Aug 2026 11.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nearly 40,000 bottles of eye drops are being pulled from store shelves across the US over concerns about potential contamination, according to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Prestige Brand Holdings, based in Tarrytown, New York , has voluntarily recalled 39,060 bottles of Clear Eyes Maximum Itchy Eye Relief eye drops because of a “lack of assurance of sterility”, an FDA enforcement report states. The FDA classified the action as a Class II recall, defined on the agency’s website as a moderate-risk situation “in which use of or exposure to a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote”. The recall specifically covers 15ml bottles carrying lot code 2552A and an expiration date of 30 September 2027. The eye drops were distributed by Medtech Products Inc, a Prestige Consumer Healthcare company. Massive egg recall in US south and south-west due to salmonella outbreak Read more Clear Eyes Maximum Itchy Eye Relief is marketed on its packaging as an astringent/lubricant redness-reliever eye drop intended to provide relief from redness, itching, burning and watery eyes. The product is sold at major retailers including Walmart, Target, Kroger, Giant Eagle, Meijer, Dollar General and Family Dollar stores. Consumers are being advised to stop using the recalled eye drops and return them for a refund. Anyone concerned about possible effects from the product is encouraged to contact a pharmacist or healthcare provider. Eye drop and other related medicinal product recalls have become relatively less common compared with the continuing food safety crisis in the US, which under the Trump administration has recently been grappling with one of the largest recorded foodborne illness outbreaks in the nation’s history. Still, eye drop recalls do happen. In 2023, for instance, the FDA recalled EzriCare Artificial Tears after the eye drops were linked to an outbreak of Pseudomonas aeruginosa , a drug-resistant bacterial contamination. That outbreak may have resulted in one death and injuries to 68 other people. A small number of those sickened had to have the affected eye surgically removed. Photograph: Li Xiang/Xinhua/AP China China expels a record number from Communist party amid Xi’s intensified purges of top officials The unprecedented number of empty seats at the fifth plenum – a symbol of expulsions – serve as a symbol for the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping Amy Hawkins in Beijing Thu 29 Oct 2026 22.56 EDT Last modified on Thu 29 Oct 2026 23.26 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering , which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping. A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year. Just 279 of the full and alternate members of the CCP’s Central Committee attended this week’s gathering, compared with the 376 originally named as members in 2022. That means that more than 25% of the original cohort were absent, many due to purges. It is the highest number of “empty chairs” at the plenum in modern Chinese history. Xi Jinping’s corruption crackdown in the spotlight as China prepares for meeting of top leaders Read more The confirmed expulsions included Zhang Youxia, the former second-in-command to China’s leader in the military hierarchy, and Ma Xingrui, the former party secretary for Xinjiang. Other absences were unexplained. “More empty seats underscores the plenum’s focus on Xi’s vision of strict internal discipline,” said Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at the Asia Society thinktank, in a post on X. The theme for this week’s plenum was party governance. Since coming to power in 2012 Xi has focused on stamping out corruption in the party. But in recent years the campaign has intensified , taking out officials in the highest ranks of the party and the military, raising questions about if the campaign is also a tool to remove political rivals or punish disloyalty. View image in fullscreen Zhang Shengming, top, sits behind Chinese leader Xi Jinping during the opening session of the fifth plenum in Beijing. Photograph: Andy Wong/AP Xi appears to have grown increasingly frustrated with what he sees as a lack of discipline in the ranks of the party that wields absolute authority over the state and society in China. Earlier this year he said that the party must uproot “sick trees” and that the fight against corruption was a “never-ending journey”. A series of purges has gutted the seven-man Central Military Commission, the ruling body of China’s People’s Liberation Army. There are now just two members left: Xi himself, and the military’s anti-graft tsar, Zhang Shengmin. Zhang was promoted to the politburo of the CCP this week, the highest ruling body in the party. Zhang is now the only military member of the senior leadership body. The plenum also laid the groundwork for the 21st Party congress, an event which happens every five years and is expected to next be held in the second half of 2027. Xi is expected to secure a fourth term as leader of the party, making him the longest ruler of Communist China since Mao Zedong. The ranks of the Central Committee and the politburo will be refreshed at next year’s congress, but many analysts believe that recent purges have been so wide-ranging that there are few suitable candidates to be promoted.
